name: Blast-Extinguishing Pellet
text: Break the pellet in your hand: anti-fire agent coats your space and all adjacent spaces. Any explosion going off there until the start of your next turn has a lower damage class. If you hold one when an explosion occurs you may break it reflexively. Also puts out tier 1 fires (other fires ignore it).

name: Bypass Boots
text: Air cushion and odd weights: stepping on a mine up to the boots' marque does not activate it.

name: Explosion Eater
text: Bagged vacuum: point it at an explosion as it occurs to absorb force and lower its damage class; the hot-air bag then floats away. Usable once.

name: Proximity Blinder
marques: mQ I proximity fuses ignore wearer
text: Proximity fuses up to the blinder's marque do not detect the wearer.

name: Ride-the-Blast Sails
text: Hidden in a hat, vest or backpack; deploys on an explosion and pulls the wearer to safety: bonus on the Dexterity roll to dodge the blast.

name: Volatile Materials Scanner
text: Bonus when trying to notice a concealed explosive on a person.

name: Acid-Spewing
text: Holds an acid that sprays everyone within or adjacent to the blast seat on detonation. 3 AP to install or switch the acid. Those in range may make a separate Dex resist to dodge the acid; acid and blast are otherwise resisted normally. (Acids: see Alchemy.)

name: After-Blast
text: Contains a second explosive that this one's detonation activates (detonates a turn later, as default, or set as a mine). Anyone in sight may roll Cunning to notice the second explosive. Each explosive is priced separately; the inner one cannot also have After-Blast.

name: Air-Lighting
marques: +1 DC per space the blast can't fill
text: Consumes air; deadlier in enclosed spaces. DC increases per space the blast would normally occupy but can't (e.g. 9-space blast in a 10×10 ft room = 4 spaces → +5 DC at mQ I). Outdoors, obstructions such as trees or low walls don't count.

name: Anti-Handling Fuse
text: After activation and once the first turn passes, anything affecting the explosive (picking up, disarming, shooting) detonates it immediately. A Sciences roll (3 AP) can bypass the mechanism (the explosive must still be dealt with afterwards); failure detonates it.

name: Automaton-Linked
marques: detonates when the linked automaton stops functioning
text: Tied into an automaton's workings; detonates immediately if the automaton is no longer 'alive'. Can be detached by disarming it; a failed removal activates it. Attaching only during a breather.

name: Clinging
text: Clings to the first thing it touches: makes an Acc roll to grab (normally a leg) and keeps grabbing unless pried off. If tossed off, it rights itself, moves on in the same direction and clings to the next thing in its path.

name: Collision-Detonated
text: Only goes off on a forceful impact: usually a fall of 100+ ft (detonates immediately), being shot out of a delivery device, or an attack made with or against it that reaches at least tier 2 damage. Otherwise never detonates.

name: Dead Man's Switch
marques: goes off when the switch is released
text: After activation you hold the switch (at least 1 turn to cook). Releasing it (0 AP) detonates it immediately, as does falling unconscious, dying, losing the arm or being disarmed of it. Turning it off costs 1 AP.

name: Depth Charges
text: Sinks to a set depth and floats there until bumped over a space. Depth set on activation or changed for 1 AP; adjusts 25 ft/turn. If the depth can't be reached (lake shallower than set), it sinks 50 ft and explodes.

name: Dirty
text: Releases a gas with the blast, filling the blast area. Inserting or switching the gas costs AP by marque. (Gases: see Alchemy.)

name: Disintegrated Remains
text: The explosive is entirely consumed; nothing remains to examine.

name: Disguised
text: Looks like something else (suitcase, potted plant, door knob; fist-sized or larger). People pass over it by default; if someone searches, it gets this bonus against their Cunning. Stacks with Concealable.

name: Engine-Detonated
text: Attached to an engine, automaton or other large moving device; detonates once the device is turned on and starts moving.

name: Entrenched
text: The mine burrows below ground; anyone stepping on the ground directly above activates it, and it drills back up and detonates.

name: Ethereal Blast
text: No visible explosion: superheated air pushes and burns everyone inside. Victims dodging don't know where the edge of the blast is.

name: Far Lobbing
text: Thrown range replaces the normal 25 ft. Throwing further: multiply this range by the Brute tier result.

name: Heartbeat-Linked
marques: detonates when wearer's heart stops or it is detached
text: Detects the heartbeat of the person it is attached to; detonates if detached or the heartbeat stops. Must be disarmed first to detach safely. Attaching only during a breather.

name: High Incendiary
text: Fires started by Incendiary are one tier higher. Tier 3 fire: 8 unsoakable fire damage per turn until 8 AP are spent putting it out; all organic, leather, cloth and wooden items are destroyed.

name: Impact
text: Goes through heat protection: negates that much of the target's heat- or fire-based damage soak against this explosion.

name: Incendiary
marques: T1 fire (2 unsoakable/turn, 2 AP to put out)
text: Everything in the blast area that fails to move or dodge catches fire. Resilient materials only get warm; the ground is unaffected unless it burns.

name: Jumping
text: Right before detonating it blasts straight up to its maximum height (or until it hits something) and detonates. If not set for next turn, it can be set to jump every turn until it hits something.

name: Leg-Spike
text: On detonation the mine makes a called shot (light weapon, DC 4) at a leg of whoever triggered it. It tries to trip: if the victim fails a Dex resist against the spike's Stk, they go prone and can't avoid the mine's explosion.

name: Line Blast
text: Instead of all adjacent spaces, the blast runs along a straight line chosen by the thrower. Range-expanding effects only lengthen the ends of the line.

name: Lingering Fires
text: Incendiary fires stay in the area and set on fire anyone or anything that moves in; fire tier as per Incendiary/High Incendiary.

name: Linked Fuse
text: All your linked-fuse explosives exchange a radio signal; if one detonates (stops sending), all detonate. Any number, but they must stay within range of each other.

name: Miniscule
text: Marble-sized; can be hidden in a mouth, a sword pommel, or used as a bullet. Bonus against being noticed when concealed; stacks with Concealable.

name: Muted
text: Barely a whisper; locating the blast by sound needs a Cunning roll. Cannot be combined with Banshee.

name: Proximity Leap
text: When something triggers its proximity fuse within range, it leaps onto the target's space and detonates.

name: Roaming
text: Default: moves once right before detonating, in a direction the activator chooses. Delayed: moves once per turn in a set direction (can't be changed without disarming). Remote-activated: the remote can steer it (1 AP, once per turn). A roaming depth charge moves until it bumps into something, then detonates. Latch/Magnetic and other 'stay in place' augments override it. A proximity fuse triggers on movement of 15 ft, so a mQ III+ roaming explosive with a proximity fuse detonates itself — use only mQ I–II.

name: Ruinous
text: Destroys everything in the blast radius (including the ground) up to that hardness tier.

name: Safe-Handling
marques: can never be set off accidentally
text: Can't be set off by squibs, remote hacking or bumping.

name: Shockwave
text: The knock back also affects everyone within this distance beyond the blast range.

name: Shrapnel
text: Victims' soak class is lowered for this attack.

name: Sinking Crater
text: The person at the blast seat must make a Dex resist or fall prone, losing their stance.

name: Sky Charges
text: Floats up to a set height and hovers until bumped over a space. Height set on activation or changed for 1 AP; adjusts 25 ft/turn. If the height can't be reached (ceiling), it hits the ceiling and explodes.

name: Super-Heated Shrapnel
text: Shrapnel sticks; at the end of the victim's next turn they take this heat damage (not soakable by normal means) unless they spend 1 AP to remove it first.

name: Target-Processing
text: Basic brainworks: activating takes 3 AP to describe who should and should not trigger it. Learnable with Pyrotechnician and Fuse Box Builder.

name: Vast Crater
marques: Sinking Crater also hits all spaces adjacent to the seat
text: Everyone adjacent to the blast seat also needs the Dex resist or falls prone, losing their stance.

name: Weaponized
marques: can be used as a weapon
text: The explosive also counts as a weapon (sword, rifle, axe…). Weapon augments may be put on it; they use explosive augment slots and are destroyed when it detonates.

name: Battlefield Scorcher
text: Adds to the range of the firebomb's Extended Blast.

name: Damaging
text: Replaces the normal 3 damage per firebomb marque.

name: Extended Blast
text: The firebomb's area is larger.

name: Lingering Fuel
text: Fuel burns longer.

name: Sparks in the Air
marques: wet or metal-armored targets can't soak
text: Pulses of electricity through the flames. Learnable with Firebomber.

name: Grasping Flames
text: Anyone moving through the fire must make a Brute resist or stop moving.

name: Magnetic Pulsing
marques: double damage to electric vehicles & fuse box automata
text: Applies when they move into the area or end their turn within it.

name: Smoking
text: Thick smoke blinds those within the area.

name: Blast Off
text: Launches everything in the target square straight up.

name: Damaging
text: Takes 2 augment slots. Replaces the normal 5 damage per squib marque.

name: Knock Back
text: Knocks anyone in the target space away from the thrower.

name: Paint Splatter
text: Paint in a color of your choice. Learnable with Squib Producer.

name: Run-Away Bomb
text: Motorized wheels: one move after hitting the ground, direction and distance of your choice.

name: Sundering
marques: one held weapon suffers a T1 sunder
text: Book says learnable with Pyrotechnician (probably meant Squib Producer).
